author: A

components.title: Compute remaining time
components.what:
Together, the pumps fill 4(1/12+1/9)=7/9 of the tank, leaving 2/9; pump B fills that in (2/9)/(1/9)=2 hours=120.0 minutes.
FINAL: 120.0

log.author: A
log.draft:
Rates: A = 1/12 tank/hr, B = 1/9 tank/hr.

Combined rate for 4 hours: 4×(1/12+1/9) = 4×(3/36+4/36) = 4×7/36 = 28/36 = 7/9 tank filled.

Remaining tank = 1 − 7/9 = 2/9.

Pump B alone finishes remaining 2/9 at rate 1/9 tank/hr:
Time = (2/9)/(1/9) = 2 hours = 2×60 = 120.0 minutes.

Check: verify 1/12+1/9 = 3/36+4/36 = 7/36 (common denominator 36 — correct since 12×3=36, 9×4=36). Then 4×7/36 = 28/36 = 7/9 (divide num/denom by 4) — correct. 1 − 7/9 = 2/9 — correct. (2/9)÷(1/9) = 2 — correct arithmetic, verifiable by cross-multiplication: (2/9)×(9/1)=2.

FINAL: 120.0

asked: The 4 hours of joint running assumes the tank does not reach full capacity before A is switched off — can you confirm 7/9 < 1 and that no overflow/cap condition applies at any point in the first 4 hours?
Does the problem's phrasing 'how many more minutes' unambiguously mean time after the 4-hour mark (not total elapsed time), and would any alternative reading change the figure?
replies: 1. Confirmed: 7/9 ≈0.7778 <1, so the tank is only 77.8% full at the 4‑hour mark; no overflow or cap condition arises during that period (rate is constant, filling is monotonic, and 4×7/36 never exceeds 1 for any t≤4h since even the full 4h total is 7/9<1). 2. The phrase 'how many more minutes' modifies the action after A is switched off, i.e., the additional time B alone needs to complete the job—exactly what was computed (2/9 tank ÷ 1/9 tank/hr = 2 h = 120.0 min). No alternative reading (e.g., total elapsed time = 4h+2h = 6h = 360 min) matches the wording 'more minutes needed,' which specifically asks for the extra time beyond the initial 4-hour period. No error found; answer stands.
